description: Renovate for the AgentLink monorepo. Supply-chain posture: cooldown before adopting new releases, no automerge, major updates and security-critical libraries reviewed by hand, GitHub Actions pinned to commit SHAs. PR titles start with DEPS (pr-hygiene rule).
Major updates wait for approval on the Dependency Dashboard

Non-runtime dev tooling (devDependencies: eslint, prettier, playwright, vitest, typescript, turbo, changesets, globals, vite and so on) in ONE weekly PR, so a week's tooling bumps touch pnpm-lock.yaml once and never rebase each other (a rebase drops the code-owner approval review-gate needs on the head commit). Security-critical packages and the S2 @types set are excluded and keep their own rules. Majors still wait for dashboard approval.
GitHub Actions digest and version updates join the same weekly dev tooling PR (workflow files are sensitive paths; the group is reviewed as a whole)
Security-critical crypto and transport dependencies (allowlisted in 04 section 8): longer cooldown, one reviewed group, labelled security-sensitive
prBodyNotes: **Security-sensitive dependency.** Read the changelog and the diff of every package in this group, check that no install scripts were added, and re-run `pnpm vectors:check`. Security class S1 or higher: an automated PR meets the review requirement only by a code owner APPROVED review on the head commit (audit-rules.md section 3).

**`@hpke/*` updates (04 section 3.3, D-66, IR-G-46-1 F-1).** The CEK wraps hand a derived ephemeral key to `@hpke/core` through its `ekm` parameter. Before any `@hpke/*` update merges, the `hpke` and `aead-envelope` vector suites must pass in every runtime (`pnpm vectors:check`: Node, Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, workerd). There is no fallback: an update that breaks them stays unmerged until a replacement is reviewed.

## Threat note

Security-critical crypto and transport dependency (S2 when the update touches packages/crypto, packages/core or packages/node; S1 otherwise). The packages in this group perform or feed the cryptography, signing and relay transport used by `@4thtech-io/crypto`, `@4thtech-io/core` and `@4thtech-io/node` (allowlisted in 04 section 8). Assets at risk: private keys, derived keys and plaintext handled in process. A compromised or buggy release could weaken key derivation, encryption or signature checks (invariants I-1 to I-4) or exfiltrate secrets (zero access rule). Supply-chain risk: a malicious release gets in-process access to all of those. Behaviour changes in any primitive must be caught by `pnpm vectors:check`.

Reviewer checklist: read the upstream changelog and release notes for the version range; confirm the lockfile diff only touches this package and its expected transitive dependencies (integrity hashes present, no unexpected new packages or registry URLs); confirm no `postinstall`, `preinstall` or `install` script was added (a PR that adds one is refused); for packages that ship native binaries or prebuilds, confirm they come from the package's own published platform packages and match the provenance and release the maintainers announce.

Residual risk: a malicious or compromised release that passes review and tests could still read keys or plaintext in process; cooldowns, lockfile integrity and the review checklist reduce, not remove, that risk. Threat model: docs/foundation/04-security-and-crypto.md section 7.

## Tests-first evidence

This is a pure dependency bump, so there is no RED commit and none is claimed (audit-rules.md section 3.4). The evidence is the full required suite on this head commit; the approver confirms it is green. A code owner (talirezun or denisjazbec) confirms this section and the Threat note by an APPROVED review on the head commit, which is how an automated PR meets the independent-review requirement (audit-rules.md section 3.3). A new approval is needed after every new commit.

description: S2 dependency: OS keychain binding used by the Node KeyStore (packages/node). review-gate classifies any PR touching packages/node as S2 and needs non-empty Threat note and Tests-first evidence sections, which Renovate regenerates with the PR body
prBodyNotes:
## Threat note

`@napi-rs/keyring` (S2: `packages/node`). It is the native binding through which the Node `KeyStore` reads and writes the owner's key material in the operating system keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Secret Service on Linux). Assets at risk: the encrypted key blobs and any secret handed to the keychain. Trust boundary: native code running as the same OS user, outside the JavaScript sandbox, with access to every keychain entry that user can read. Abuse cases: a malicious release reads or exfiltrates keychain entries, writes entries under attacker control, or logs secrets; an API or error-semantics change makes `KeyStore` fail open (for example returns an empty value as "not found" and creates a new key). Supply-chain risk is highest here because the package ships prebuilt native binaries per platform.

Reviewer checklist: read the upstream changelog and release notes for the version range; confirm the lockfile diff only touches this package and its expected transitive dependencies (integrity hashes present, no unexpected new packages or registry URLs); confirm no `postinstall`, `preinstall` or `install` script was added (a PR that adds one is refused); for packages that ship native binaries or prebuilds, confirm they come from the package's own published platform packages and match the provenance and release the maintainers announce.

Residual risk: a malicious or compromised release that passes review and tests could still read keys or plaintext in process; cooldowns, lockfile integrity and the review checklist reduce, not remove, that risk. Threat model: docs/foundation/04-security-and-crypto.md section 7.

description: S2 dependency: local SQLite store used by packages/node
prBodyNotes:
## Threat note

`better-sqlite3` (S2: `packages/node`). It is the native SQLite binding behind the local `Store` (messages, approvals, publisher lease, outbox). Assets at risk: stored ciphertext metadata, approval decisions and their integrity. Abuse cases: a malicious release reads or exfiltrates the database or its contents; a behaviour change in transactions, compare-and-set or schema handling breaks approval or lease guarantees. The package compiles or downloads a native addon at install time: check how the binary is obtained and that no new install script or download host appears.

description: S2 dependency: WebSocket client used by packages/node
prBodyNotes:
## Threat note

`ws` (S2: `packages/node`). It carries the relay and local approval-server WebSocket traffic of the Node package. Assets at risk: traffic metadata and ciphertext in transit (content stays end-to-end encrypted). Abuse cases: a malicious release redirects, logs or modifies traffic, or weakens TLS or origin checks (SSRF and realpath rules in 04 section 4 still apply); a parser or framing regression lets an untrusted peer crash or confuse the process (inbound content is untrusted, I-5).

Reviewer checklist: read the upstream changelog and release notes for the version range; confirm the lockfile diff only touches this package and its expected transitive dependencies (integrity hashes present, no unexpected new packages or registry URLs); confirm no `postinstall`, `preinstall` or `install` script was added (a PR that adds one is refused); for packages that ship native binaries or prebuilds, confirm they come from the package's own published platform packages and match the provenance and release the maintainers announce.

description: Type definitions for S2 packages/node: same S2 body notes so review-gate (d) passes
prBodyNotes:

Type definitions used by `packages/node` (S2 by path). They ship no runtime code, but a changed type can hide a behavioural mismatch with the real library. Reviewer checks: the changelog; the lockfile diff (integrity hashes, no unexpected packages or registry URLs); no install script added; typecheck and the full suite green on the head commit.
